dervis-irab:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا أَنْصارَ اللَّهِ) كونوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, the wāw is its noun (ism), and أنصار الله is its khabar (predicate); the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) to أنصار. It has also been read أنصارا لله, in which case لله would be a naʿt (adjective) of أنصارا. (كَما قالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ لِلْحَوارِيِّينَ مَنْ أَنْصارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ) The grammarians have disagreed greatly about this kāf, and the upshot of what they have mentioned is that it admits three possibilities:
1- It is in the position of accusative on the implication of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "We said that to them, just as ʿĪsā said."
2- It is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); it has been said that this is questionable, since they are not being commanded to "be a being".
3- It is speech construed according to its meaning rather than its wording, and this is the view al-Zamakhsharī inclined to, for he said: «If you ask: what makes the comparison sound, when its apparent sense is a comparison of their being helpers with ʿĪsā's saying "Who are my helpers unto Allah?" I answer: the comparison is construed according to the meaning, and on that basis it is sound; what is meant is: be helpers of Allah just as the disciples were helpers of ʿĪsā when he said to them, "Who are my helpers unto Allah?"».
The meaning of أنصاري إلى الله, and the transitivity of this word with إلى, has already been discussed in Āl ʿImrān. من is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and أنصاري is the khabar; إلى الله is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "heading towards the support of Allah". What follows is the text of al-Zamakhsharī's words: «If you ask: what is the meaning of His saying من أنصاري إلى الله? I answer: its meaning must correspond to the disciples' reply when they said "We are the helpers of Allah", and what corresponds to it is that the meaning be: who are my troops heading towards the support of Allah? The annexation in أنصاري is different from the annexation in أنصار الله, for the meaning of "We are the helpers of Allah" is "We are those who support Allah", whereas the meaning of من أنصاري is "Who, among the helpers, are those who are particular to me and will be with me in supporting Allah?" It is not sound for its meaning to be "Who will support me along with Allah?", because that does not correspond to the reply; and the proof of this is the reading of those who read: من أنصار الله».
(قالَ الْحَوارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنْصارُ اللَّهِ) قال الحواريون is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the الحواريون are his chosen ones, and they were the first to believe; the discussion of this word has been given in detail earlier. نحن is a mubtadaʾ and أنصار الله a khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). It is a case of annexing a descriptive (waṣf) to its object, i.e. "We are those who support Allah", that is, His religion [Translator's note: the source prints «دنيه», evidently a misprint for «دينه» "His religion"; translated accordingly].
(فَآمَنَتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ وَكَفَرَتْ طائِفَةٌ) The fāʾ conjoins to omitted clauses which must be supplied, i.e. "When ʿĪsā was raised to heaven, people split into two factions concerning him, so a faction believed"; طائفة is the fāʿil of آمنت, and من بني إسرائيل is a naʿt of طائفة; وكفرت طائفة is conjoined to فآمنت طائفة.
(فَأَيَّدْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلى عَدُوِّهِمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا ظاهِرِينَ) The fāʾ likewise conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "so the two factions fought one another". أيدنا is a verb and its fāʿil, الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); على عدوهم is attached to أيدنا. فأصبحوا is conjoined to فأيدنا; the wāw is its noun and ظاهرين its khabar, i.e. "prevailing, overpowering".

dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَقْتاً): [Al-Zamakhsharī] said in al-Asās: «مقته مقتا: it is hatred arising from an ugly matter; and in this connection a man's marrying his stepmother [Translator's note: the source has "رابّته", strictly "his stepdaughter"; the usual expression refers to marrying the father's wife] was called نكاح المقت (the marriage of loathing): «إنه كان فاحشة ومقتا». And مقت إلى الناس مقاتة, like بغض بغاضة (he became hateful to people); he is ممقوت and مقيت.»
(مَرْصُوصٌ): stuck together, one part upon another, as if built with lead (al-raṣāṣ). It has been said: المرصوص is that whose parts are joined together and level; it has also been said: bound with lead; and it has been said: the compacted, from تراصّ الأسنان (the teeth being set close). In al-Miṣbāḥ: «الرصّ is the joining of parts of a building to one another and its firmness; its pattern is that of ردّ.» Among the remarkable features of rāʾ and ṣād, when they occur as the first and second radicals of a word, is that they indicate the meaning of compactness and firmness, and of readiness for a matter. You say رصدته, ارتصدته and ترصدته: I sat for him on his way, watching for him; and تراصد الرجلان (the two men watched for each other). Dhū al-Rumma said:
يراصدها في جوف حدباء ضيق ... على المرء إلا ما تخرّق حالها
(He lies in wait for them inside a narrow, humped [hide], tight upon a man except where its state has been torn.)
And سبع رصيد: a beast of prey that lies in wait to spring. "I am lying in wait for you (أنا لك بالمرصد والمرصاد)", i.e. you will not escape me. "I have prepared (أرصدت) this army for fighting, this horse for the chase, and this money for paying dues", when you have made it ready for that and put it in its way. رصع التاج: he adorned the crown with stars of ornament; رصّع الطائر عشه بالقضبان والريش: the bird brought the twigs and feathers of its nest close together and wove it; أسنانه مرتصعة مرتصّة: his teeth are set close; تراصع العصفوران: the two sparrows mated; and راصع الطائر أنثاه: the bird mated with its female. رصف الحجارة ورصّفها: he set the stones close together; the water ran over الرّصف and الرّصاف, which is laid rock; تراصفوا في الصلاة والقتال: they stood in close ranks in prayer and in fighting; and you say: تراصفوا ثم تقاصفوا (they closed ranks, then crowded upon one another); رصف إحدى قدميه إلى الأخرى: he put one of his feet close to the other; تراصفت أسنانه تراصفا, which is their being set in rows. And figuratively: امرأة رصوف, a woman narrow in the private part; and رجل رصيف, a man firm in his work; and it is said: he gave an answer that was مترّص [Translator's note: so in the source, presumably مُتْرَص, "firmly made"], حصيف (sound), بين (clear), رصيف (firm) — neither feeble nor light. رصن البناء وغيره رصانة: it was firm, so it is رصين; and figuratively: he has a رصين (sound) opinion, and كلام متين رصين (solid, firm speech).

* I'rab:
(سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): the i'rab of this verse has preceded at the opening of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, so renew your acquaintance with it.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَ تَقُولُونَ ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ): لم: the lām is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun conveying disapproval and rebuke. It has preceded that when a preposition enters upon interrogative ما its alif is dropped, as in بم, فيم, مم, إلام, علام, عمّ and حتام; the alif was dropped only because ما and the preposition resemble a single thing. Its use with the alif dropped has occurred frequently in the speech of the questioner, and the original form has come in use rarely. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تقولون; تقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ما is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لا is negating; and the clause تفعلون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.
(كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ تَقُولُوا ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ): كبر is a past verb, i.e. it is grave; مقتا is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil; عند الله: the adverb is attached to an omitted adjective of مقتا, or [to an omitted] ḥāl (circumstantial); and أن تقولوا is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of كبر. The original is "the loathing of their saying became grave", i.e. the loathing consequent upon their saying what they do not do. It is also permissible that كبر be of the category of نعم and بئس, so the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun explained by the indefinite tamyīz, and أن تقولوا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause before it, since it is the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm). The discussion of all that has preceded, and further discussion of this construction will come in the section on rhetoric.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ): إنّ and its noun, and the clause يحب is its predicate; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause يقاتلون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; it is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; في سبيله is attached to يقاتلون; صفا is a ḥāl from the wāw in يقاتلون; كأنّ and its noun, and بنيان is its predicate; مرصوص is a naʿt (adjective) of بنيان; and the clause is a second ḥāl, from the pronoun in صفا, because it means "ranging themselves", so it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila).

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «كبر مقتا عند الله أن تقولوا ما لا تفعلون» there is intensification and repetition, and for this reason this clause has been considered among the most eloquent of speech and the most effective in its meaning, for several reasons:
1- He intended wonder without the form of wonder (taʿajjub), to magnify the matter in the hearts of the hearers, because wonder is only at something that breaks with custom and with its like.
2- He attributed [the verb] to أن تقولوا and put مقتا in the accusative as its explanation, to indicate that their saying what they do not do is pure loathing with no admixture in it.
3- The choice of the word المقت, because it is the most intense and extreme hatred, so much so that the expression "the marriage of loathing" was used, as preceded in the section on vocabulary.
4- Then He was not content to make the hatred great, but made it the most intense and the most outrageous; and His saying عند الله is more effective than that, because if the greatness of its loathing in the sight of Allah is established, its greatness and intensity are complete, and doubts about it are dispelled.
5- The repetition of His saying ما لا تفعلون, which is one expression in one statement. Among the benefits of repetition are inspiring awe and magnifying; otherwise the speech would have been complete if it had been said "كبر مقتا عند الله ذلك", so its repetition is only for the sake of this benefit.
2- The inclusion of the specific under the general. The general prohibition of speech not supported by action has come, and what is intended is the inclusion of the specific matter that came after it, which is His saying: «إن الله يحب الذين يقاتلون في سبيله صفّا كأنهم بنيان مرصوص». In His mentioning that immediately after the general prohibition there is evidence that the loathing attached to the saying of those who promised steadfastness in fighting the disbelievers and did not fulfil it — just as you say to one who has committed a particular offence: "Do not do what brings shame upon you, and do not revile Zayd." The benefit of such a construction is prohibiting the one thing twice, once included in the general and once singled out specifically; and this is better than prohibiting it specifically twice, for that is counted among the good kinds of repetition [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense seems to require "among the kinds of repetition", i.e. the specific-twice option is mere repetition], whereas this is not repeated, besides the magnification and awe that the generalisation carries.

dervis-irab:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ يا قَوْمِ لِمَ تُؤْذُونَنِي وَقَدْ تَعْلَمُونَ أَنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ): a resumptive statement brought to console His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and to settle him upon patience. إذ is the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember); the clause قال is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; موسى is the fāʿil (agent); لقومه is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قال. لم: the lām is a preposition and ما an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive by the lām; the secret of dropping the alif of interrogative ما when a preposition precedes it has preceded. تؤذونني is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The wāw is circumstantial; قد is a particle of realisation, even though it has entered upon the imperfect — the imperfect was used only to indicate the continuation of the state. تعلمون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; أني رسول الله is أنّ with its noun and its predicate, and أنّ with what lies in its scope fills the place of the two objects of تعلمون; إليكم is attached to رسول; and the clause وقد تعلمون etc. is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning is that whoever honours Allah honours His Messenger.
(فَلَمَّا زاغُوا أَزاغَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ): the fāʿ is conjunctive; لما is linking or temporal (ḥīniyya); زاغوا is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause أزاغ الله قلوبهم has no grammatical position; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause لا يهدي القوم الظالمين [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has الفاسقين] is the khabar (predicate).
(وَإِذْ قالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ يا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ): the adverb is the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر"; the clause قال is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; عيسى is the fāʿil; ابن مريم is a badal (substitute) of عيسى; يا بني إسرائيل is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf. He did not say "O my people" because he had no tie of lineage to them, since he had no father, and lineage is only from the father's side, even though his mother Maryam was among the noblest of them in lineage. إنّ and its noun, and رسول الله إليكم is its predicate, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ وَمُبَشِّراً بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِي اسْمُهُ أَحْمَدُ): مصدّقا:
a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in رسول الله, since it is interpreted as مرسل (sent). لما is attached to مصدقا; the adverb is attached to an omitted [word] with no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; يدي is annexed to بين, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is dual; مبشّرا is conjoined to مصدّقا, so it is a ḥāl like it; برسول is attached to مبشّرا; the clause يأتي is an adjective of رسول; من بعدي is attached to يأتي; اسمه is a mubtadaʾ and أحمد its khabar, and the clause is a second adjective.
(فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ قالُوا هذا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ): the fāʿ is resumptive; لما is linking or temporal; جاءهم is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; بالبيّنات is attached to جاءهم; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position; and the clause هذا سحر مبين, made of the mubtadaʾ and khabar, is in the position of the accusative as the object of their saying.

* Benefits:
The scholars of Arabic say that قد accompanies the past to bring it close to the present; from this is the muezzin's saying قد قامت الصلاة (the prayer has [just] been established). Its accompanying the past also contains the meaning of expectation; that is why Sībawayh said: قد فعل is the answer to لمّا يفعل (he has not yet done); and al-Khalīl said: this statement is for people who are waiting for it. As for [its use] with the imperfect, it conveys paucity, like ربما, as in their saying: إن الكذوب قد يصدق (the liar sometimes tells the truth). So since its meaning with the imperfect is paucity, and in the verse it has entered upon an imperfect, the right explanation is that this is of the kind of speech by which they intend excess in the opposite of what [the form] expresses; قد in this sense is the counterpart of ربما in His saying «ربما يودّ الذين كفروا لو كانوا مسلمين», for there it is more effective than كم in expressing abundance. Just as ربما was used for abundance, contrary to its original meaning of paucity, so is the use of قد here, to express the abundance of their knowledge, i.e. the realisation of its emphasis, contrary to its original meaning of paucity.

dervis-irab:7-13.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُوَ يُدْعى إِلَى الْإِسْلامِ): the wāw is resumptive; من is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, i.e. "no one", in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); أظلم is the khabar (predicate); ممّن is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أظلم; the clause افترى is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; على الله is attached to افترى; and الكذب is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). وهو: the wāw is circumstantial; هو is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يدعى is the khabar of هو, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); i.e. his Lord calls him, on the tongue of His Prophet, to Islam, in which lies the happiness of both abodes, and in place of answering it he fabricates lies against Allah. يدعى is an imperfect verb in the passive, and إلى الله [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has إلى الإسلام] is attached to يدعى.
(وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يهدي is the khabar; القوم is the mafʿūl bihi and الظالمين is a naʿt (adjective) of القوم.
(يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِؤُا نُورَ اللَّهِ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ): يريدون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ليطفئوا: the parsers have mentioned several views on this lām, the strongest being three:
1- That it is added to the object of the will. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Its original is يريدون أن يطفئوا, as came in Sūrat Barāʾa. It is as if this lām was added with the verb of willing as an emphasis of it, because of the meaning of will it carries in your saying جئتك لإكرامك (I came to you to honour you), just as the lām was added in لا أبا لك as an emphasis of the meaning of annexation in لا أباك.» Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, supporting this view: «The lām in ليطفئوا is an emphasising lām that has entered upon the object, because the implied form is يريدون أن يطفئوا.»
2- That it is the lām of causation and the object is omitted, i.e. they want the nullification of the Qur'an, or the removal of Islam, or the destruction of the Messenger, in order to extinguish.
3- That it is in the sense of accusative أن, and that it puts the verb in the accusative by itself. Al-Farrāʾ said: The Arabs put the lām of kay in place of أن after أراد and أمر; and al-Kisāʾī also held this.
The wording of Abū Ḥayyān, after citing the aforementioned sayings of al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya — he said: «What Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned, that this lām mostly attaches to the object when it is fronted, is not the most frequent; rather, زيدا ضربت is more frequent than لزيد ضربت. As for their saying that the lām is for emphasis and that the implied form is أن يطفئوا, so that the extinguishing is the object of يريدون, it is not the school of Sībawayh and the majority.»
(وَاللَّهُ مُتِمُّ نُورِهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكافِرُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; الله is a mubtadaʾ, متمّ the khabar, and نوره the muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of يريدون or of يطفئوا. The wāw is also circumstantial; لو is conditional; كره الكافرون is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl from the preceding ḥāl clause, so it is overlapping (mutadākhila); the answer of لو is omitted, its implied form being "He completes it and makes it prevail".
(هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ): هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its khabar; the clause أرسل is the ṣila; رسوله is the mafʿūl bihi; بالهدى is attached to أرسل or to an omitted ḥāl; دين الحق is conjoined to الهدى; the lām is for causation; يظهره is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its noun are attached to أرسل; على الدين is attached to يظهره; كله is a tawkīd (emphasis); the clause ولو كره المشركون is a ḥāl; the object of كره is omitted, i.e. its being made to prevail; and the answer of لو is also omitted, its implied form being "He makes it prevail".
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى تِجارَةٍ تُنْجِيكُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ): هل is an interrogative particle whose meaning is informing and affirmation, i.e. "I will guide you"; He put it in the form of a question only to arouse eagerness and kindle desire. أدلكم is an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil being latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنا", and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; على تجارة is attached to أدلكم; the clause تنجيكم is an adjective of تجارة; من عذاب is attached to تنجيكم; and أليم is an adjective of عذاب. The account of its revelation, which is impossible [Translator's note: so in the source, "الممتنع"; presumably a misprint for "الممتع", "enjoyable"], will come in the section on benefits.
(تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ): the clause is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is: you believe", or resumptive, in answer to an implied question, as if it were asked: What is the trade? تؤمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative, but in the sense of a command; this is indicated by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: آمنوا بالله ورسوله وجاهدوا. The benefit of shifting from the command to the statement is to signal the obligation of compliance, as if they had complied, so He informs of a faith and a jihad that exist. بالله is attached to تؤمنون; رسوله is conjoined to بالله; تجاهدون is conjoined to تؤمنون; في سبيل الله is attached to تجاهدون or to an omitted ḥāl; بأموالكم is attached to تجاهدون; and أنفسكم is conjoined to أموالكم.
(ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ): ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ and خير the khabar; لكم is attached to خير; إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause تعلمون is the predicate of كنتم; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then do it"; and the object of تعلمون is omitted for brevity, since it is known, i.e. that it is better for you.
(يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ): يغفر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request understood from His saying تؤمنون, as preceded. It has also been said that it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you do it, He will forgive". The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «يغفر لكم: there are two views on its jussive. One: it is the apodosis of an omitted condition indicated by the speech, its implied form being "if you believe, He will forgive you", تؤمنون being in the sense of آمنوا. The second: it is the answer to what the question indicates, the meaning being "will you accept, if I guide you?" Al-Farrāʾ said it is the answer to the question according to the wording; but this is far-fetched, because His guiding them does not necessitate forgiveness.» The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «If you say: does al-Farrāʾ's saying that it is the answer to هل أدلكم have any justification? I say: its justification is that the object of the guiding is the trade, and the trade is explained as faith and jihad; so it is as if it were said: Will you trade in faith and jihad? He will forgive you.» Ibn al-Munayyir commented on it, saying: «He only justified al-Farrāʾ's parsing in the way he mentioned because, if he had made it the answer to His saying هل أدلكم — "for if I guide you to such-and-such, I will forgive you" — the forgiveness would then follow from the mere fact of His guiding them to good; and it is not so: forgiveness follows only from their doing what He guided them to, not from the guiding itself. So هل أدلكم على تجارة was not interpreted [Translator's note: reading "أوّل" as "أُوِّل"] as "will you trade in faith and jihad" except so that forgiveness would follow from the doing of faith and jihad, not from the guiding. But this interpretation is not needed, for when the gist of the speech comes to "Shall I guide you? I will forgive you", it joins the likes of the saying of Allah the Exalted: «قل لعبادي الذين آمنوا يقيموا الصلاة», for He made the performing of prayer follow from the command to it, as if He said: for if you say to them "establish [prayer]", they will establish it.»
(وَيُدْخِلْكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): يدخلكم is conjoined to يغفر, and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري is an adjective of جنات; من تحتها is attached to تجري; and الأنهار is the fāʿil.
(وَمَساكِنَ طَيِّبَةً فِي جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ): مساكن is conjoined to جنات; طيبة is an adjective of مساكن; and في جنات عدن is a second adjective.
(ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the forgiveness and admission into the gardens; الفوز is the khabar and العظيم an adjective of الفوز.
(وَأُخْرى تُحِبُّونَها نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌ قَرِيبٌ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw
is a conjunction; أخرى is a postponed mubtadaʾ and its fronted khabar is omitted, i.e. "you have another blessing or reward". It may also be accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and He grants you another", the clause تحبونها being an adjective of أخرى; or accusative by an implied verb explained by تحبونها, so that it is of the category of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the governor), and in that case the clause تحبونها is not an adjective, because it explains the governor before أخرى. نصر is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "that other blessing is help from Allah", or a badal (substitute) of أخرى if you parse it as a mubtadaʾ; من الله is an adjective of نصر; فتح is conjoined to نصر; and قريب is an adjective. وبشّر: the wāw is conjunctive and بشّر is an imperative verb, conjoined to تؤمنون because it has the sense of a command, as preceded.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله» there is an allegorical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), representing their state in striving to nullify the truth by the state of one who blows at the light of the sun with his mouth to extinguish it, in mockery and derision of them. It has also been said that the metaphor is explicit (taṣrīḥiyya), and the extinguishing is a tarshīḥ (consolidation of the metaphor).

* Benefits:
Muqātil said: This verse — «يا أيها الذين آمنوا هل أدلكم على تجارة تنجيكم من عذاب أليم» up to His saying «وبشّر المؤمنين» — was revealed concerning ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn. That was because he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If you would permit me, I would divorce Khawla, become a monk, castrate myself, forbid myself meat, never sleep at night and never break my fast by day." He ﷺ said: "Marriage is part of my sunna, and there is no monasticism in Islam; the monasticism of my community is only jihad in the way of Allah, and the castration of my community is fasting. Do not forbid the good things Allah has made lawful for you. Part of my sunna is that I sleep and stand [in prayer], break my fast and fast; whoever turns away from my sunna is not of me." ʿUthmān said: "I wish, O Prophet of Allah, that I knew which trade is most beloved to Allah, so that I might trade in it." Then [the verse] was revealed.
